title: CTV Advertising That Reaches the Right Rooms | Qujam

facts.fact: Qujam states that on its self-serve platform advertisers can launch CTV campaigns with no daily minimums.
facts.quote: On a self-serve platform like Qujam, advertisers can launch campaigns with no daily minimums

facts.fact: Qujam claims that enterprise ad-tech platforms Simpli.fi and managed-service agency Propellant Media still enforce high monthly minimums for CTV access; this is the vendor's own characterization, and no specific dollar amount is given.
facts.quote: While some enterprise ad-tech platforms like Simpli.fi or managed-service agencies like Propellant Media still enforce high monthly minimums for CTV access

facts.fact: Qujam claims that enterprise programmatic platforms such as Simpli.fi and Agility often require massive minimum spends, with no specific amount stated.
facts.quote: massive programmatic platforms like Simpli.fi and Agility, which offer robust CTV inventory but often require massive minimum spends

facts.fact: Connected TV (CTV) is defined as television content watched through an internet-connected device such as a smart TV, streaming stick, gaming console, or set-top box.
facts.quote: Connected TV, or CTV, refers to television content watched through an internet-connected device.

facts.fact: Over-the-top (OTT) is defined as the broader category of streamed video content delivered over the internet.
facts.quote: while over-the-top, or OTT, is the broader category of streamed video content delivered over the internet.

facts.fact: Traditional broadcast TV buying relies on broad geographic markets called DMAs and demographic estimates.
facts.quote: Traditional broadcast TV relies on broad geographic markets (often called DMAs) and demographic estimates.

facts.fact: Qujam says traditional TV measurement relies on broad reach estimates such as Nielsen ratings or overall seasonal sales lift.
facts.quote: Traditional TV relies on broad reach estimates, like Nielsen ratings or overall seasonal sales lift

facts.fact: The Qujam article was published on September 24, 2026.
